newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower, Chicago spread active.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower, Chicago spread active.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower on a break in CBOT wheat, but inter-market spreading, mainly MGE/CBOT activity, underpinned the market, traders said.
"It was mostly inter-market spreading, Minneapolis/Chicago," a trader said.
They said LFG Futures did two million bushels of MGE March/CBOT March and Cargill Investor Services and Benson Quinn were net buyers of one million bushels of the March.
Wheat markets, including Minneapolis spring wheat, were pressured by disappointing exports of U.S. wheat.
USDA early Thursday said for the week ended January 9 U.S. net export sales of wheat totaled 177,500 tonnes, below expectations for 200,000 to 400,000 tonnes.

The futures downturn occurred after the market was buoyed early by harsh winter weather in the U.S. which is slowing movement of wheat and boosting spot cash basis markets, traders said. Cash spring wheat merchandisers said nothing was moving because of the weather.
MGE spring wheat futures closed unchanged to one cent per bushel lower, with March down one at $3.94-1/4.
